For most **single or queen electric blankets that cycle on and off**, I’d choose a **1 kWh power station**, such as the **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2**. One guide estimates its 1,024 Wh battery can run a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, though actual runtime depends on the blanket’s settings and how often it heats ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)).

If you want a more conservative choice for a blanket that draws heavily or runs close to full power, step up to the **Jackery HomePower 3000**. One estimate says a queen blanket averaging 260 W needs about 2,600 Wh for eight hours, and lists this model as sufficient ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/)).

**Rule of thumb:** check the blanket’s wattage, then allow extra capacity for inverter losses. A 1 kWh station is a reasonable pick for a typical cycling blanket; for roughly 260 W sustained through the night, look closer to 3 kWh. Plug the blanket directly into the station, and keep the station off the bed. ([Sunbeam guidance, via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night))
